subject.title: Tailscale serve mode lacks optional secondary authentication

question: Should verified Tailscale Serve identity remain a standalone Control UI/WebSocket auth path, or should OpenClaw add an opt-in layered shared-secret requirement on top of it?
rationale: This changes a public Gateway authentication contract and security boundary, so code inspection can show the gap but cannot choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Design layered auth
options.body: Add a named opt-in secondary-auth contract with config/schema/docs, warning or audit coverage, WebSocket auth enforcement, and tests.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Keep verified Tailscale identity as the tokenless path and document `gateway.auth.allowTailscale: false` as the shared-secret-only deployment mode.

options.title: Docs and audit only
options.body: Improve visibility of the trust boundary without adding a new auth mode or config option.

recommendation.title: Design layered auth
recommendation.body: Add a named opt-in secondary-auth contract with config/schema/docs, warning or audit coverage, WebSocket auth enforcement, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history on the Tailscale/gateway auth hardening path and merged no-auth exposure fix.
